name: Beaminster Tunnel
facts: Beaminster Tunnel, a 345‑foot brick passage, opened on 29 June 1832 after just over two years of construction, dramatically easing travel by flattening a 1‑in‑6 gradient to a gentler 1‑in‑10.
Engineered by Michael Lane, a colleague of Marc Brunel, the tunnel was one of Britain’s first road tunnels and remains the only pre‑railway road tunnel still in use today.
In July 2012 a torrential rainstorm triggered a landslide that partially collapsed the north entrance, tragically burying a vehicle and killing two motorists, prompting costly remedial work.
